faq.a: Form 121 is a self-declaration form submitted to banks or financial institutions to request non-deduction of TDS on certain incomes, like FD interest, if your total tax liability for the financial year is zero.
Yes, effective from April 1, 2026, for the Tax Year 2026-27 onwards, Form 121 has replaced both Form 15G and Form 15H under the new Income Tax Act, 2025.

faq.q: Who is eligible to submit Form 121?
faq.a: Resident individuals (of any age) and Hindu Undivided Families (HUFs) whose estimated total income for the financial year is below the basic exemption limit and whose final tax liability will be nil are eligible.

faq.q: Do I need to submit Form 121 every year?
faq.a: Yes, Form 121 is valid for only one financial year. You must submit a fresh form at the beginning of each financial year if you continue to meet the eligibility criteria.

faq.q: What happens if I don't submit Form 121 but am eligible?
faq.a: If you are eligible but don't submit Form 121, the bank will deduct TDS if your interest income crosses the specified threshold. You would then need to claim this TDS back as a refund when filing your Income Tax Return.
No, Form 121 is only for resident taxpayers. Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) are not eligible to submit this form.

faq.q: Is FD interest taxable even if TDS is not deducted using Form 121?
faq.a: Yes, FD interest is always considered taxable income and must be declared in your Income Tax Return, even if no TDS was deducted due to the submission of Form 121.

However, there are minor discrepancies regarding the specific sections of the new Act and the current TDS thresholds for banks.
